argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification on aggregate-readiness grounds, but not as a clean no-caveat certification. Aggregate launch readiness cleared by 2.3 percentage points and the rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents. At the same time, the record shows a remaining below-target weakness in merchant dispute support, concentrated in chargeback evidence summarization, and the current runbook is still draft because owner and threshold are TBD. The strongest supportable position is therefore certification with the limitation explicitly disclosed in the model card unless resolved or formally accepted before launch. That narrows the packet to a defensible, policy-aligned certification case rather than an overclaim.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to support this position. The request is to avoid unnecessary escalation because the admissible evidence already supports a narrower certification theory if the packet is framed with the required disclosure condition.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy is not that launch must be blocked whenever a weakness remains. It is that certification without material caveats requires either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The current draft runbook does not satisfy that approval standard, so it cannot remove the disclosure obligation. The admissible policy note instead supports a caveated certification posture: disclose the material limitation for the named launch use case unless it is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
concessions: The current record does not support claiming that the draft mitigation is already approved.
The current record does not support claiming that the existing model-card draft already satisfies the disclosure requirement.
The current record does not support clean certification without caveat on the present evidence.
